1.explanation: The root cause is that the copy-paste logic does not carry over the Boundary Event’s attachedToRef reference to the new Task. In BpmnCopyPaste.js the paste handler only resolves default sequence-flow references, but never re-wires the attachedToRef property on boundary events. Moreover, in ModdleCopy.js references (including attachedToRef) are skipped by default, so the copy process omits the attachment entirely. Fixing requires extending BpmnCopyPaste.resolveReferences to handle attachedToRef and/or adjusting ModdleCopy so that attachedToRef is explicitly copied and re-connected to the new Task business object.
1.bug_scenario: In the attached replay you can see a user drawing a simple BPMN Task with a Boundary Event attached to its right side. When they select both the Task and its Boundary Event and perform a copy / paste, the Task is duplicated and positioned to the right, but the Boundary Event—although duplicated—no longer stays attached to the new copy of the Task. Instead it floats freely, losing its attachedToRef association.
